messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: High tail latency & cache miss spike detected for prefix-caching service in us-west-2. p95 ~ 420ms -> 980ms, p99 ~ 1.8s -> 4.6s over last 10m. Error rate for streaming endpoints increased from 0.2% -> 2.7%. Correlates with deploy 2567000021 (prefix-hash change).

sanjay: seeing it in traces too — streaming stalls with many requests hitting 'cache miss' path and then contending on paging. KV-store IO queue depth spiking on shards 7/12.

miguel: confirmed. prefix hit rate dropped from 87% -> 21% for production traffic. Prefetch workers saturated, backpressure into runtime.

tara: any customer-facing 5xxs?

sanjay: yes — a small subset of customers on dedicated clusters reported increased 503 for streaming connect timeouts (tickets #CS-8192, #CS-8195). Not global but high QPS tenants impacted.

ops-bot: Deploy 2567000021 rolled out to 30% of hosts at 08:13 UTC. Canary passed on synthetic traffic but missed distribution of long-tail prompts.

miguel: root cause hypothesis: prefix hashing introduced a new salt ordering that changed prefix partitioning, invalidating warmed caches across many shards leading to hot cold starts + increased paging. Also prefetch logic assumes stable prefix mapping; it now misses frequently.

tara: mitigation steps we should try now: 1) rollback prefix-hash change 2) enable conservative fallback cache (per-tenant sticky prefix) 3) increase prefetch worker pool temporarily 4) route high-tail traffic to dedicated fallback model variant. Thoughts?

carol: +1 for rollback. Rolling back is fastest to restore hit rate. We can also warm caches proactively after rollback.

sanjay: prepping rollback plan. Command to roll back the service:
```bash
kubectl -n inference rollout undo deploy/prefix-service --to-revision=2567000008
```
I'll push approval and start at t+3m if no objections.

miguel: while rollback proceeds, do we have quick mitigations to reduce customer impact? Can we enable a temporary in-memory TTL override to accept stale prefix hits?

tara: yes — runbook has a flag `PREFETCH_ALLOW_STALE=true` we can flip in the config map for runtime; that will allow more cache hits at cost of slightly stale KV prefixes.

sanjay: flipping now on a single shard as experiment. Command: 
```bash
kubectl -n inference patch cm runtime-config --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/PREFETCH_ALLOW_STALE","value":"true"}]'
```
Applying to shards 7/12 first.

miguel: also increasing prefetch workers:
```bash
kubectl -n inference scale deploy/prefetch-workers --replicas=24
```
I've queued that, will monitor CPU.

eva: watching metrics: after applying stale-allow and scale to shard 7, p95 fell 20% on that shard within 2m, overall p95 reduced ~15%. p99 still high.

carol: good signal. Start rolling stale-allow onto shards in sequence (7,8,9) to avoid thundering herd.

ops-bot: Rollout undo started for deploy/prefix-service at 08:37 UTC by sanjay.

sanjay: rollback progressed to 60% at 08:42 UTC, health checks passing on rolled hosts. Cache hit rate starting to climb on rolled shards.

miguel: note — we need to avoid full cache purges during rollback; warmup will be needed. Will schedule background prefetch job to replay recent prefix keys: `internal-prefetch replay --window 30m --shards 0-11`.

tara: customer impact summary for CS: 
- Affected tenants: 7 mid-market customers, 3 enterprise customers on long-sequence streaming (IDs redacted)
- Symptoms: elevated streaming connect timeouts (503), increased completion latency causing some client-side retries (amplifying load)
- Mitigation: staged rollback + PREFETCH_ALLOW_STALE + scaled prefetch workers reduced errors for impacted tenants.

miguel: running prefetch replay now; ETA ~ 14m to sufficiently warm top prefixes for whole cluster.

eva: metrics update 08:55 UTC: global prefix hit rate 21% -> 64% as rolled hosts come up. global p95: 420ms -> 260ms. p99: 4.6s -> 1.2s. Error rate down to 0.6%.

sanjay: rollback completed at 08:58 UTC. Verifying no regressions. Paging IO queue depth trending down.

carol: start drafting post-incident notes. Immediate actions: revert prefix-hash change from code review, add e2e test that simulates long-tail prompt distributions, add canary with long-tail traffic, and update runbook to include PREFETCH_ALLOW_STALE as emergency knob.

miguel: follow-ups for eng-runtime: 
- Hardening prefetch to tolerate transient prefix remapping.
- Add metric alert for sudden drop in prefix hit rate (>30% delta in 5m).
- Consider adding a staged key-warmup after any prefix mapping change.

tara: handoff to night oncall @miguel. Miguel — please keep monitoring p99 and watch for any residual streaming stalls. Runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/prefix-prefetch-mitigation

miguel: acknowledged. I'll keep an eye and post updates every 30m until stable. Escalate to SRE if p99 > 2s for >10m.

ops-bot: Incident ticket created: INC-2026-0198 (priority P1) — linked to CS tickets #CS-8192, #CS-8195.

sanjay: RCA notes to follow in postmortem. Quick summary for now: deploy introduced prefix partitioning change that caused warmed caches to be invalidated in production; mitigation via rollback + stale-allow + prefetch scaling restored hit rates and reduced SLO breaches.

carol: adding runbook tasks and owners in the postmortem draft — assigning follow-ups to @sanjay (rollback safety checks), @miguel (prefetch resilience), @eva (dashboards/alerting).

miguel: one more: patch incoming to add a canary harness that replays long-tail prompt traces during canary phase to catch this class of regressions. Will open PR and tag for review.

tara: thanks everyone. If you are taking action items, drop them here. I'll close the live incident channel once stable for 30m.

sanjay: action items in thread: 
- sanjay: postmortem + revert PR (ETA 24h)
- miguel: prefetch robustness PR & canary harness (ETA 72h)
- eva: alert + dashboard updates (ETA 48h)
- carol: customer comms summary with CS (ETA 3h)

miguel: night oncall logging in. will update if anything flares. :white_check_mark:

ops-bot: oncall-handoff: miguel is now oncall for incidents (start 09:12 UTC).

carol: closing note: no data exfiltration or security concern observed. All logs show normal auth flows.

sanjay: thanks all. I'll start drafting the incident timeline and link artifacts (deploy diffs, prefetch logs, kv-queue graphs).

miguel: acknowledged. Monitoring baseline for the next 2h.

oncall-bot: Incident stable — moving to monitoring phase. If p99 stays < 1.5s and errors < 0.5% for 30m, we'll mark resolved.
